answers.district_name: Agua Fria Union High School District
answers.student_ai_age_gate: No age gate inside the high school span; students may use only the district-approved AI tools (Gemini, the Gemini notebook tool and Canva) and about fifty other AI sites are blocked for students. Ninth graders get mandatory lessons on evaluating AI critically.

answers.ai_review_structure: Software and online services need Technology approval before use on district devices, and a new web resource needs both Academics (instructional value, curriculum fit, accessibility) and Technology (privacy, security, integration, cost); either can veto. Staff-built tools go through the innovation office, and every production deploy waits on the Director of Innovation's approval (a named backup can click).

answers.teacher_ip_notes: Under discussion, not adopted: the builder keeps the intellectual property and the district keeps a free perpetual licence, pending legal review.
answers.data_tiers: The district's self-hosted model is preferred for work over student records; a hosted model may receive student data only under a district agreement that covers it (the enterprise ChatGPT workspace is the first). Apps send counts and keys, not values, to assistants by default; no student names in code repositories; nothing personal is retained or learned from.
answers.builder_pathway: The Builder's Permit: an invite-only, roughly fifteen-hour asynchronous course of three modules (FERPA and Arizona privacy, district policy, security, GitHub, sign-on), each passed at 80 percent, ending in a GitHub capstone a human reviews. The permit unlocks GitHub Copilot and, after a month's notice, is required to author Apps Script.
answers.app_launch_review: A pull request in a private district repository, CI green, an adversarial review by a second AI agent, a human merge, then the Director of Innovation's approval at the production environment gate; health check, rollback on failure, and an accessibility scan of the pages touched. Rollout is staged: the innovation office, about five testers at one campus, one whole school, then everyone.
answers.mcp_details: Role-checked read tools over the district's reporting warehouse (roster, attendance, struggling-student flags, assignment scores, intervention placements, campus summaries), resolved server-side to the signed-in user's scope: a teacher sees only students they teach, campus administrators their campus. Served to the enterprise ChatGPT workspace, a district portal and the self-hosted model; writes stay in the district's own apps.
agents_in_production: Admin Data Agent: campus administrators ask questions about their own campus on the self-hosted model
District data connector: teachers query their own students from the enterprise chat workspace
Weekly headless audit that checks the shared agent skills against live systems and pushes factual fixes

Daily job-fleet digest with a model-assisted advisory on what changed

answers.secrets_handling: Passwordless by default: each app runs as its own directory service identity with Windows-integrated database access and no password in any config. Model tokens are per caller, shown once, never pasted into an AI, and rotated (not re-minted) on exposure. Remaining secrets live in a team password manager; a pre-commit hook and CI secret scans block credentials in repositories.
answers.promotion_path: Prototype on the builder's machine against an empty local database, or as a single page in the reviewed ideas sandbox; then a development copy on its own host, deployed by a non-administrator runner; then production after a merge to main and the Director of Innovation's approval at the deploy gate. A good prototype is either folded into an existing district tool or given its own hosted app, after a privacy review.
answers.ownership_handoff: Tools live in the district's GitHub organization with code owners, so a departure does not orphan them; the innovation office takes over sign-in, security review and data feeds when a prototype is adopted, and the builder keeps shaping it. Records name roles, never people, and a departing role holder follows a dated handoff (handoff docs, an assistant built on them, access reduced on schedule).

answers.cost_controls: Compute is treated as a finite resource: general staff are on the fast default model in the ChatGPT workspace with costlier features off, the heaviest users are steered to Gemini, student-data work prefers the self-hosted model, and new automation tools start as free-edition pilots with no budget line.
answers.biggest_win: A district MCP server where the permission check lives in the tools, not the model: teachers ask about their own students from the enterprise chat workspace and administrators about their own campus on a self-hosted model, and a question outside their scope returns nothing because the tool refuses.
